results.name: Marie-Madeleine
results.description:
Marie-Madeleine, Jan Borreman (attributed to), Brabant, Brussels, circa 1490-1500, Brussels hallmarks, oak, traces of polychromy. Musée du Cinquantenaire (Brussels, Belgium). Made with ReMake and ReCap pro from AutoDesk.

The same expressions, grace, reserve and mastery of this sculpture are found in Saint George, especially in the decapitation scene.

For more updates, please consider to follow me on Twitter at @GeoffreyMarchal

results.name: Sainte Marie-Madeleine tenant un vase à parfum
results.description:
Lorraine, 1400-1430

Sainte Marie-Madeleine tenant un vase à parfum
Proviendrait d'une église de Verdun.
calcaire, traces de polychromie et de dorure
Saint Mary Magdalene holding a perfume vase
Probably from a church in Verdun.
Limestone, traces of polychrome and gilding 
Donné en 1858 à l'abbé Mangin, curé d'Ancemont. Vendue le 12 mai 1906 par l'abbé Lecourtier, curé d'Ancemont. Acquis de l'Office des biens et intérêts privés (l'œuvre ayant été séquestrée et ayant fait l'objet d'un procès), 1922

Musée du Louvre
RF 1774

Cette statue de Marie-Madeleine faisait probablement partie d'une Mise au Tombeau ou de la Déploration du Christ. 
This statue of Mary Magdalene was probably part of a group representing the Entombment or Lamentation of Christ.

results.name: Bison De La Madeleine
results.description: Petite statuette de 10.5 cm de longueur découverte en France à "La Madeleine en Tursac" en Bordogne. Il s'agit d'une objet en bois de renne d'environ 15000 ans AP. C'est la ville de "La Madeleine" qui a donné son nom à l'époque Magdalénienne (17000 à 12000 ans AP). La statuette représente un bison à la tête retournée qui se lèche le flan.

results.name: Usine Ste Madeleine Sugar Factory
results.description:
In 1870 Ste. Madeleine was taken over by the Colonial Company, a British Conglomerate, that built the first modern factory there during the process of “Centralisation” which reduced the number of smaller and less efficient works in favour of a larger, modern and more efficient factory.Ste. Madeleine was surrounded by several estates. There was Belle Vue to the north, Cedar Hill to the east, St Charles to the south and Petite Morne to the west. As time went on, many of these estates were taken over by the Colonial Company and then the New Colonial company, that came later (in 1895). Prior to nationalisation, New Colonial Co Ltd in 1913 became the Sainte Madeleine Sugar Co Ltd. It was once reputed to be ‘the finest factory in the West Indies’.
